name: Reedvile Anchorage
desc: Super quiet, big, easy anchorage with very little traffic and few crab pots. Excellent protection from all directions. The very best place to anchor just south of the Potomac.

name: Little Choptank Anchorage
desc: Lots of sholing getting in, but Defiant made it all the way into this very quiet cove. Excellent protection from the north and I'd assume most other directions - you are really back there. The bank is steep but I was able to take Bash to the edge and throw him up to poop via dinghy.

name: Wye River Anchorage
desc: Lots of safe little places back here to hide out, protection from all sides. Quiet, not much easy shore access but enough to toss the dog up and let him poop.

name: Little Bay Anchorage
desc: Big, calm, very protected, and tons of beach access to walk the dog. I’ve stayed here a few days and no matter what the bay is doing the water is glass here. Crab pot hell getting in and out.

name: Solomons Island Anchorage
desc: Infamous town anchorage, good for about 3 boats. Public dinghy docks, tiki bar, and a cute little town to walk the doggo. Zero provisions - people come here to party and eat ice cream, that’s it. Loud party scene at night in the summer, quiet and old white people country club vibe in the fall and winter.

name: Great Bridge Lock
desc: Opens every hour on the hour. Coordinated with the Great Bridge just south so you pass through both. Must call on 13 to request tie-up. Arrive 20 minutes after the hour when heading south. Call the lock on VHF 13 (or 757-547-3311) as you approach. Give your boat name and direction, and say you’re requesting a southbound lockage. Hold position outside until you get the green light or the tender waves you in. The tender will tell you which side to tie up on. Rig fenders and have bow and stern lines ready on both sides, since you won’t know which side until you’re called in. The chamber is 72' x 600' with fixed bollards for tying off.
